_metadata.methodology: Web search and medical data aggregation using high-authority sources.

hemoglobin.description: A protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

wbc.description: Cells that help the body fight infection.

platelets.description: Cells that help the blood clot.

rbc.description: Cells that carry oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.

hematocrit.description: The proportion of red blood cells to the total volume of blood.

alt.description: An enzyme found mostly in the liver; high levels can indicate liver damage.

ast.description: An enzyme found in the liver and heart; high levels can indicate liver or muscle damage.

creatinine.description: A waste product produced by muscles; high levels indicate impaired kidney function.

bun.description: Measures the amount of nitrogen in your blood that comes from the waste product urea.

sodium.description: An electrolyte that helps maintain water balance in and around your cells.

potassium.description: An electrolyte that is important for heart and muscle function.

calcium.description: A mineral that is important for bone health and nerve function.

cholesterol.description: The total amount of cholesterol in your blood.

ldl.description: Often called 'bad' cholesterol because it can lead to plaque buildup in arteries.

hdl.description: Often called 'good' cholesterol because it helps remove other forms of cholesterol.

triglycerides.description: A type of fat (lipid) found in your blood.
